title: The Gothic Novel
objective: After this level you can explain the Gothic toolkit of old castles, buried secrets and dread, from Walpole to Dracula.
summary: The Gothic novel began with Walpole's Castle of Otranto (1764), posed as an old manuscript. Its toolkit of castles, trapdoors, secrets and dread runs through Radcliffe to Stoker's Dracula (1897).

cards.headline: The first Gothic novel opens with a giant helmet crashing down out of nowhere.
cards.body: It crushes the lord's son, Conrad, on his wedding day. That's how Horace Walpole's The Castle of Otranto begins. Published in 1764, it is generally regarded as the first Gothic novel, and it started a fashion for dread.

cards.headline: A fake old manuscript
cards.body: Walpole didn't sign it. The first edition claimed to be a translation of an old Italian manuscript, printed in Naples in 1529, and only the second edition admitted he'd written it. The genre's name looks backward too: such fiction is called Gothic because its imagination came from medieval buildings and ruins. The past itself was the haunted house.

cards.headline: The toolkit
cards.body: Gothic novels reuse a kit of parts: castles or monasteries with underground passages, dark battlements, hidden panels and trapdoors, all soaked in mystery and terror. Ann Radcliffe, whose The Mysteries of Udolpho (1794) made her England's most popular novelist, added a twist of her own. Her seemingly supernatural events turn out to be natural, but only after a long, delicious wait.

cards.headline: The castle comes to town
cards.body: By 1897 the kit could travel. Bram Stoker's Dracula is told mostly through its characters' own diaries and journals, and its Transylvanian vampire makes his way to England. The Gothic had come home to England.

cards.headline: The Gothic: unlocked
learned: It posed as an old Italian manuscript

questions.prompt: Put these Gothic novels in order, from earliest to latest.
questions.explanation: The Castle of Otranto came out in 1764, The Mysteries of Udolpho in 1794, and Dracula in 1897.

questions.prompt: How does Ann Radcliffe build suspense in The Mysteries of Udolpho?

options.label: Ghosts appear openly on the first page
options.rationale: She keeps the mystery going instead.

options.label: She tells the reader the ending first
Each chapter closes with a moral stated in plain words
Seeming ghosts are explained as natural, but late

questions.explanation: Radcliffe's seemingly supernatural events are revealed as natural only after a long delay, which keeps readers in suspense.

questions.prompt: Like a legend, Otranto was presented as if it were history. What did Walpole's first edition claim to be?

options.label: A diary kept by a vampire hunter
A ballad sung by Italian villagers
options.rationale: It claimed to be a manuscript.

options.label: A report in a London newspaper
A translation of an old Italian manuscript

questions.explanation: Walpole passed the novel off as the translation of an Italian manuscript printed in Naples in 1529, much as a legend is told as a matter of history.
